control.objective: Test whether 4h trade intensity works as a FILTER on the existing long-only strategy: skip entries whose 4h trade-intensity percentile (trades vs the trailing 20-bar average) is above a threshold. Sweep thresholds (no filter / p90 / p75 / p50), report trades kept, net R/t with 95% CI, and gross R/t, split by regime (2023, 2024, 2025-26, ALL). The signal to test is NEGATIVE: high intensity predicted LOWER forward returns (non-overlapping IC -0.160, z=-1.90), so the filter should REMOVE high-intensity entries.
control.notes: VERIFIER SIGN-OFF: npm test passes 7/7. intensityfilter.mjs implementation is sound: self-contained simulation with perfect byte-for-byte alignment to backtestMultiTF (verified cross-check across all 20 pairs, no divergence). Sample integrity clean: 6,397 pooled entries, only 6 excluded (<0.1%), no n<30 at any threshold. Result conclusive: filtering high-intensity entries does NOT improve R/t at any threshold in any regime — CIs overlap throughout. Expected: high intensity → LOWER forward returns, so removing it should help. Actual: all thresholds flat-to-worse (2023 -0.256→-0.324, 2024 -0.375→-0.388, 2025-26 -0.455→-0.465). No suspicious pattern (huge R/t jump on tiny sample). Conclusion sound: trade-intensity-as-filter is closed, IC's economic size is below strategy's R variance.
